claims.explanation: E01/E02 and evidence/tables/table2_main_results.md contain test-accuracy means/spreads and LBCS coreset sizes for all three datasets at k=1000,2000,3000,4000. A best-baseline relation can express accuracy >= all seven baselines, but the equally required strict final-size < k compares a measured size against numeric configuration labels, not another reported measurement. No reported-evidence relation accepts those literal per-row size bounds or evaluates a coordinate as a numeric operand. Copying k into fake evidence or omitting size would narrow the conjunction; neither is done. The weaker falsifier involving lower accuracy than all baselines does not replace the stronger best-baseline statement.

A single best_baseline_consistency property compares LBCS mean test accuracy against every other method in evidence/tables/table3_lbcs_sizes.md, for all four configurations in each of F-MNIST, SVHN and CIFAR-10 (84 paired comparisons). ge preserves highest mean and the falsifier any baseline higher, including ties, rather than imposing a significance test or strict superiority from the title. Table 3 conditions and E01 step 7 identify these as baseline reruns at LBCS-selected sizes, not the original fixed-k Table 2. Source row/section labels are retained verbatim: F-MNIST k=2000 says approximately 1935 in its row but 1915 in its section and Table 2; no correction or equality of those sizes is asserted. The declaration tests all same-row accuracy comparisons under the reported equal-size protocol, not an independently verified exact size mapping.

The statement is an almost-sure asymptotic epsilon-optimality theorem under Progressable and Stable Moving conditions, with a minimum over the feasible masks. E03 and evidence/tables/table5_ablation_search_times.md provide only finite T=100 through 2000 empirical accuracy/size observations. The installed relations cannot express a probability-one limit, the two formal assumptions, or the constrained global optimum. Finite empirical convergence or decreasing size is not substituted for Theorem 2.

E04 requires all seven baselines at all four k values under 30% noise, 50% noise and imbalance. evidence/figures/fig2_imperfect_supervision.md and figure2_imperfect_supervision.md tabulate approximate accuracy only for 30% noise and class imbalance (and disagree in the approximate readings). evidence/tables/table7_imperfect_supervision.md and table6_imperfect_supervision_sizes.md include 50% noise only for coreset SIZE, not accuracy. The referenced Figure 4 accuracy results for 50% noise are not included as numeric evidence in this fixed ARA. Thus the full three-condition accuracy claim and the epsilon-compromise overfitting mechanism cannot be discharged by checking the two available conditions.

E05 and evidence/tables/table4_imagenet.md contain ImageNet-1k Top-5 scores at predefined 70%/80% ratios and optimized ratios 68.53%/77.82% in parentheses in the LBCS cells. Public evidence parsing exposes only the primary accuracy values 89.98/90.84, not either parenthetical selection ratio as an addressable measurement. The claim independently asserts those exact optimized ratios and the falsifier requires optimized < predefined; reported pairwise relations do not provide literal ratio-equality/bound checks either. An accuracy-only best-baseline property would omit this essential size condition. Influential is unreported rather than assigned a made-up score.
